newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open down, tobacco firm Seita falls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open down, tobacco firm Seita falls.

text.p: French stocks opened lower in quiet trading on Monday, the day of the monthly settlement.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 14.18 points, or 0.51 percent, at 2,742.86 at 0830 GMT, and the CAC-40 June futures contract was 17 points lower at 2,738.

Shares in tobacco company Seita fell 1.68 percent to 186.80 francs on the huge U.S. tobacco settlement struck on Friday. "There's a feeling that governments may develop a common policy toward tobacco," a broker said.
Stock in LVMH, which is expected to keep buying Grand Met shares in a bid to foil the planned Grand Met-Guinness merger, also underperformed the market, shedding 1.5 percent to 1,508 francs.
